chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Ẓarīf, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

For a tooth, there are five camels, whether it is the frontmost of them or the rearmost, and that is one-half of one-tenth of the diyah. If the diyah is in dinars, then dinars; if it is in dirhams, then dirhams; if it is in cattle, then cattle; if it is in sheep, then sheep; and if it is in camels, then camels, on the basis that the diyah is two hundred cows. And for a tooth there are ten cows, and for a finger there is one-tenth of the diyah: ten camels.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.السِّنِّ: a tooth, for which a specific diyah is assigned
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, used here as a standard unit of diyah compensation
key_terms.الْإِصْبَعِ: a finger, for which one-tenth of the diyah is assigned
key_terms.الْبَقَرِ: cattle, a compensatory valuation category for diyah
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver dirhams, another form in which diyah may be paid
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold dinars, one form in which diyah may be paid
key_terms.غَنَمًا: sheep, another compensatory valuation category for diyah

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a tooth or a finger in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out fixed diyah amounts for bodily injuries, specifying compensation for a tooth and a finger. It also indicates that compensation follows the currency or property standard in which the diyah is assessed, such as dinars, dirhams, cattle, sheep, or camels.
